reuse.why: Every month-wide action, including the new one, takes its categories from getMonthBudgetCategories/shouldIncludeMonthBudgetCategory, and the new action reuses averageToBudgetAmount and the sheet's sum-amount cells.

duplication.why: The hidden rule moves out of the 'average' SQL into the single predicate; the only repetition is the goal_def column added to both getBudgetData and the selection queries and the boilerplate flag threading.

placement.why: The selection rule stays in month-action-categories.ts and the new action sits with its siblings in actions.ts and app.ts.

scope.why: Focused on the month-wide actions; it drops the 'zero' hidden exception without comment and leaves the action parameter unused in the predicate.

maintainability.why: The rule is in one place, but callers pass a positional undefined for previousMonth to reach the new flag, the now-unused action parameter lingers, and the new action borrows the 'average' label.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All month-wide actions route through shouldIncludeMonthBudgetCategory (copyPreviousMonth directly, the rest via getMonthBudgetCategories)

disguised_duplication.where: No reshaped copies; the new action follows the existing per-category loop pattern via shared helpers

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthBudgetCategories and shouldIncludeMonthBudgetCategory gain an includeHiddenCategories flag threaded positionally after an undefined previousMonth at every call site; the action argument becomes dead
